chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Do not eat the meat of al-jallālah animals, and if any of their sweat touches you, then wash it."

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: The garment is to be washed specifically from the droppings of chickens, and it is not obligatory to wash it from the droppings of pigeons and other birds whose meat is halal to eat, as we have explained. What indicates this has already passed in what preceded, and this also indicates it.

key_terms.اللُّحُومَ الْجَلَّالَةَ: the meat of animals that feed on filth
key_terms.عَرَقِهَا: their sweat, treated here as requiring washing upon contact
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it; an instruction to purify what was affected

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating al-jallālah animals and washing impurities from their sweat or bird droppings?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the impurity and consumption of al-jallālah animals, forbidding their meat and requiring washing if their sweat comes into contact with a person. It also includes al-Shaykh's legal clarification regarding bird droppings, distinguishing between chickens and other halal birds in rulings of taharah.
